subject: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners
messages:
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Aisha.Kapoor@finfo.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:20:00Z
Subject: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the bake-off runs.

Call summary (short):
- Win condition: match CloudAI accuracy at <= 2x unit cost and P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token prompts
- Primary workloads: transaction summarization + entity extraction (mixed request sizes)
- Success criteria: quality parity on prompts in the shared eval set (F1/ROUGE delta < 2 pts), P95 latency target above, and stable throughput of 250 req/s sustained for 10m window

Proposed test scope & owners:
- Redwood baseline (no quant) + Redwood-optimized (4-bit quant + KV cache) — owner: ben.carter
- Hyperscaler baseline (CloudAI managed endpoint) — owner: finprocurement/CloudAI POC
- Scoring & evaluation matrix (accuracy, latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, memory spikes) — owner: marissa.cole

Timeline suggestion:
- Confirm priorities & procurement contact by EOD Mon (11/30)
- Dry-run (internal) 12/6 — validate runbook and data access
- Official comparative runs 12/9–12/12
- Results review / decision 12/15

Attachments:
- finfold-test-matrix.csv (matrix + prompts)
- redwood-vs-cloudai-runbook.md (test steps + env)

Ask: please confirm the above priorities and add any missing success criteria. Also share the person on procurement/security who will own account setup for CloudAI access.

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha.Kapoor@finfo.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Chris.Lowe@finprocurement.com
Date: 2026-11-28T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Thanks Rafael — this is a great summary.

Couple clarifications from my side:
- Please include P95 and tail-99 latency targets — 99th < 450ms is important for low-throughput bursts
- For accuracy, add business-critical prompts (top 20) that must be exact matches where applicable
- We want to include a 3rd run: CloudAI + their optimized config + a reseller vendor image (our legal team asked)

Procurement/security: looping in Chris Lowe (cc) — he'll share the procurement contact and any AD/SSO requirements. We can share a Google Drive folder with the eval prompts — link: https://drive.google.com/finfold/bench-scope

We'll confirm by EOD Mon but proceed with your timeline if that helps keep momentum.

Best,
Aisha

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Thanks — a few tactical suggestions from the SE side:

1) Redwood differentiators to highlight during review:
   - Predictable latency shaping + graceful fallback to smaller variants
   - Built-in KV prefix caching for repeated transaction patterns (can cut P95 by ~20% in our last benchmark)
   - Cost controls: per-route batching & token caps for burst protection

2) Test matrix notes:
   - Add a column for 'warm vs cold' to capture KV cache priming effects
   - Include tokenization parity check (same tokenizer + sequence lengths)

3) Owners / deliverables:
   - Ben: prepare two model configs (baseline / rwood-opt) + run scripts
   - Me: evaluation harness & scoring script (will publish results as a CSV)
   - Rafael: coordinate procurement + schedule dry run

Attaching a lightweight test-case template (redwood-test-case-template.md) — put real prompts into the shared Drive.

-marissa

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Quick technical plan from my side:

- Run definitions:
  * baseline: standard FP16 / default batching
  * redwood-opt: 4-bit quant (GPTQ-ish) + KV cache warmup + continuous batching policy tuned to 20ms max latency

- Metrics capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, memory (GPU) over time, and error rates
- Edge case tests: long prompt (2k tokens), concurrency ramp (50->300 req/s in 60s), and token-privacy regression check
- Artifacts I will drop in the Drive:
  * runbook: redwood-vs-cloudai-runbook.md
  * raw logs tar: run-20261109-redwood-baseline.tar (placeholder stub)

I'll aim to have configs + test scripts ready by 12/4 so we can do an internal dry run 12/6.

-ben

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Aisha.Kapoor@finfo.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, Chris.Lowe@finprocurement.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Aisha — perfect. We'll proceed with the expanded scope and add the 99th percentile latency and the reseller run you requested.

Next steps on timing:
- 11/30 EOD: you confirm procurement contact (Chris, can you please share?)
- 12/4–12/5: we finalize configs internally
- 12/6: internal dry run
- 12/9–12/12: official comparative runs (we'll timebox each run and publish interim logs)
- 12/15: results review presentation (we'll bring a short slide deck + CSV of results)

I attached the proposal draft for procurement to kick off the PO process (proposal-draft.docx) and the test matrix CSV.

If procurement is ready earlier we can accelerate the official runs; otherwise we stick to these dates.

Thanks,
Rafael

Attachments: proposal-draft.docx (application/msword), finfold-test-matrix.csv (text/csv)

From: Aisha.Kapoor@finfo.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Chris.Lowe@finprocurement.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: FinFold competitive bench: scope, success criteria, and owners

Hi Rafael,

All set — Chris is our procurement lead and will start the PO/Docusign flow. Contact: Chris Lowe (chris.lowe@finprocurement.com). He has OK'd the timeline and will provision CloudAI test access by 12/5.

DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope12345
Drive folder shared: https://drive.google.com/finfold/bench-scope

We'll see you for the dry run on 12/6. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Best,
Aisha
